title: At the Airport
author: Léxi
desc: Enregistrement, contrôle des passeports, porte d'embarquement : tout ce qu'il faut dire.

p: Fatou is flying from Abidjan to New York to visit her cousin. It's her first time on a plane.
"Good evening. Where are you flying to today?"
"To New York."
"Can I see your passport and your ticket, please?"
"Here you are."
"Thank you. How many bags are you checking in?"
"One bag. And this small bag is my hand luggage."
"Please put your bag on the scale. Twenty-two kilos, that's fine. Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat?"
"A window seat, please!"
"Here is your boarding pass. Your gate is B12. Boarding starts at ten forty-five."
Ten hours later, Fatou arrives in New York. She goes to passport control.
"Good afternoon. What's the purpose of your visit?"
"I'm visiting my cousin. And I'm on holiday."
"How long are you staying?"
"Three weeks."
"Where are you staying?"
"At my cousin's house, in Brooklyn. Here is the address."
"Do you have a return ticket?"
"Yes, here it is. I'm going back on the twentieth of August."
"OK. Welcome to the United States. Enjoy your stay!"

*Where is gate B12?* — Où est la porte B12 ?
*My flight is delayed.* — Mon vol est retardé.
*I missed my flight.* — J'ai raté mon vol.
*I lost my bag.* — J'ai perdu mon sac.
*Where is the baggage claim?* — Où est le retrait des bagages ?
*Where can I find a taxi?* — Où puis-je trouver un taxi ?
Practise: imagine you are travelling to London. Answer these questions: *Where are you flying to? How long are you staying? What's the purpose of your visit?*
